title: Test whether a similarity is a valid kernel
brief: Compute the smallest eigenvalue of a Gram matrix, find the squared length of a combination of points, and use both to build a positive semidefinite test.
hints: min_eigenvalue only needs np.linalg.eigvalsh(K)[0]. eigvalsh returns real eigenvalues in ascending order for a symmetric matrix, so the first one is the smallest.
combination_squared_length is v @ K @ v. For K = Phi Phi^T it equals the squared norm of Phi^T v, which is why it can never be negative for a real feature map.
is_psd has three steps: return False if K is not square, return False if np.allclose(K, K.T, atol=tol, rtol=0.0) fails, then compare the smallest eigenvalue with -tol. A zero eigenvalue is allowed.
